updates.scope_and_remaining_work: The noncommutative input is integrated at the printed finitely generated left-module scope. For any left ideal I contained in Ring.jacobson R, the actual submodule equality N ⊔ I • top = top implies N = top. No commutativity, Noetherian, semisimplicity, finite length, or two-sidedness of I is required for this lifting theorem. The proof derives the radical lifting result from maximal submodules and the ring-radical action inclusion, rather than assuming the desired conclusion.

The complete generating-set/family equivalence and canonical cardinal seedRank equality are proved for arbitrary unital rings and finitely generated left modules using the literal M / (Jac(R) • top), its actual scalar action over R / Jac(R), and an exact quotient-map kernel. Any lifts of a generating quotient family generate upstairs, and both minimum-cardinality inequalities are established. The natural seedFinrank equality is proved as well. No semisimplicity hypothesis is needed. The descriptive semisimple-top sentence is covered by the pinned general IsSemisimpleRing.isSemisimpleModule instance applied to this actual quotient module. This is not an algorithm for computing the radical or finding generators.

The local formula is proved for noncommutative local rings and finitely generated left modules. From IsLocalRing R the source proves uniqueness of the maximal left ideal, identifies the actual Jacobson radical as maximal, constructs DivisionRing (R / Jac(R)) internally, and proves the canonical seedRank equals the left vector-space Module.rank of the actual radical quotient. The natural finite-rank equality is also proved. No commutative residue-field surrogate or caller-supplied division-ring certificate is used.

Split-field certificate transport remains proved. Block 07 supplies the complete radical/top generator-number reduction over arbitrary unital rings, so that reduction is no longer a missing input. The division-ring matrix-factor generator formula, the general regular-module multiplicity equivalence, abstract Wedderburn/module decomposition integration, and final exact formula assembly remain. A residue-division-ring formula for local rings is not a proof of the matrix/product formula for all semisimple Artinian rings.
